forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Edges up to 21%. In late-May 2026 Hassabis sharpened his timeline to 'AGI is 3 to 4 years away' and now treats 2029 as a live possibility, while Amodei maintains his 2026-27 'powerful AI' thesis and Legg holds ~50% for minimal AGI by 2028. The horizon is increasingly within the resolution window, but the bar (a credible lab announcement OR 3+ leading researchers stating AGI is achieved) is still unmet and there is no agreed definitional threshold.
forecasts.base_rate: No clean reference class for a technology being universally declared 'general intelligence'. Lab-CEO timelines (2026-2030) have a poor calibration record and behave as upper-bound predictions.

factors_up.factor: Hassabis tightens his estimate to a 3-4 year horizon, putting AGI inside the pre-2030 window
AI-accelerated research compounds capability gains across frontier labs

factors_down.factor: No consensus definition of 'AGI achieved'; resolution criteria (announcement OR 3+ researchers) unmet
Aggregate professional-forecaster mass sits in 2027-2033, with little probability in the next 12 months

key_uncertainties: Definitional threshold for declaring 'AGI'
Whether 3+ leading researchers would jointly state AGI achieved
Lab incentives to declare AGI for commercial/regulatory reasons
update_triggers: Coordinated researcher statement that AGI is achieved
Benchmark saturation across general reasoning suites

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Edges up to 27%. June 2026 reporting confirms McKinsey's ~10% cut (3,000-4,000 roles, headcount down from a 45,000+ peak) is the largest since 2008 and partly AI-attributed, with revenue growth stalled and Accenture, KPMG, PwC, EY, Deloitte and Bain all cutting since 2023; over 150,000 tech/corporate roles have gone globally in 2026 with consulting near the top. The structural shift is now unmistakable, but cuts remain concentrated in back-office and junior research and are still an order of magnitude below the 33% revenue-or-employment bar by 2030.
forecasts.base_rate: Major professional-services sectors rarely contract 33% in value or employment within ~5 years absent a systemic shock; historical analogues eroded margins gradually rather than collapsing headcount.

factors_up.factor: McKinsey's ~10% cut is its largest since 2008 and explicitly AI-linked; peers cutting in parallel
Clients increasingly using in-house AI tools, eroding the traditional consulting value proposition

factors_down.factor: Cuts so far (~10%) are far below the 33% threshold and concentrated in support roles
Firms are redeploying into AI-implementation advisory, partly offsetting displaced demand

key_uncertainties: Whether 2+ credible analyses would attribute a ≥33% decline primarily to AI
Pace of AI substitution vs. new AI-advisory demand
Revenue vs. employment - which metric crosses the threshold first
update_triggers: A top-tier firm announces cumulative cuts approaching 33%
Published analysis attributing sector-wide ≥33% decline to AI
Sustained multi-year revenue contraction across MBB

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Holds at 5%. The mid-June 2026 PollCheck average is essentially unchanged: Reform UK ~27.6%, Labour ~18.7% level-pegging the Conservatives ~18.7%, with Greens ~13.6% and Lib Dems ~12.0%. Reform has led since late 2025 and Starmer's ratings remain weak. With the next election not due until 2029 there is time for recovery, but Labour is running third-equal and would need a large, sustained swing to become the largest party.
forecasts.base_rate: Governing parties trailing by ~9pts at mid-term sometimes recover, but a third-placed governing party regaining plurality is historically rare under FPTP.

factors_up.factor: Election up to ~3 years away (by Dec 2029) leaves ample time for reversion
FPTP can convert a modest vote recovery into a seat plurality if the right splits

factors_down.factor: Reform's sustained double-digit lead since mid-2025; Labour level with Conservatives in third-equal
Persistently weak leader ratings for Starmer

key_uncertainties: Election timing within the 2029 window
Durability of the Reform surge
Whether the centre-left vote consolidates behind Labour
update_triggers: Sustained Labour recovery to within a few points of the lead

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Edges up to 80%. Hassabis's late-May tightening to a 3-4 year horizon, alongside Amodei (2026-27), Legg (~2028 for minimal AGI) and Suleyman (human-level on most professional tasks by 2027), means the 2035 window comfortably contains nearly all credible timelines. AI-accelerated AI research strengthens the case that the threshold is crossed within ~9 years; the main drag remains the definitional/declaration requirement rather than capability.
forecasts.base_rate: Expert aggregate distributions place majority probability mass before 2035; long-horizon tech-arrival forecasts are more reliable than short-horizon ones.

factors_up.factor: Multiple lab leaders now forecast AGI well within the decade (Hassabis 3-4 yrs)
Compounding AI-assisted research shortening capability-improvement cycles

factors_down.factor: Definitional/declaration risk: capable systems may exist without a recognised 'AGI achieved' statement
Possible scaling plateaus, compute/energy constraints, or regulatory slowdown

key_uncertainties: Whether capability gains continue compounding or plateau
Definitional consensus on AGI
Compute, energy and regulatory constraints over the decade

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Holds at 8%. The US intelligence community's 2026 Annual Threat Assessment reiterates that Beijing has no fixed timeline and is not planning a 2027 invasion, prefers unification without force, and judges an amphibious assault extremely difficult. China's buildup continues 'steady but uneven', and gray-zone quarantine/encirclement rehearsals keep a non-trivial chance of an event meeting the >72hr blockade bar, but the central assessment remains firmly against a near-term initiation.
forecasts.base_rate: Cross-strait crises have stayed below the threshold of a sustained blockade or assault for decades; great-power initiations of major blockades/invasions are low-frequency events.

factors_up.factor: Gray-zone 'quarantine' framing lowers China's perceived escalation threshold

factors_down.factor: US IC assesses no current plan or fixed timeline; Beijing prefers non-force unification
Self-deterrence: a blockade would cripple the fabs China's economy depends on

key_uncertainties: Whether a 'quarantine' would satisfy the >72hr blockade resolution
Xi's risk tolerance and internal timeline
US/allied deterrence posture
update_triggers: Declared quarantine or coast-guard interdiction regime
Major shift in US deterrence signalling

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Jumps to 44% (from 13%). The May 2026 CPI release came in at exactly 2.0% - the BoE target for the first time since 2021 and down sharply from 2.8% in April. The headline now sits right at the threshold with clear disinflation momentum, so dipping below 2.0% in at least one of the remaining prints (June-November 2026) is now close to a coin-flip. The offset is sticky underlying inflation: core was 3.5% and services 5.7% in May, which historically slows the final descent and could keep the headline at or just above 2.0%.
forecasts.base_rate: Headline CPI sitting exactly at 2.0% with downward momentum has frequently undershot target for at least one month in past disinflation episodes, though sticky services inflation often arrests the descent near target.

factors_up.factor: May print at 2.0% (down from 2.8%) puts the headline right at the threshold with momentum
~6 monthly releases remain before Jan 2027, multiple chances to undershoot

factors_down.factor: Sticky core (3.5%) and services (5.7%) inflation can hold the headline at/above 2.0%
Autumn energy-cap and base effects could nudge the headline back up

key_uncertainties: Persistence of services and wage inflation
Energy and food price path through H2 2026
Sterling and import-price effects
update_triggers: A monthly CPI print at or below 2.0%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Rises to 76%. With ~6 weeks to the confirmed 31 July 2026 release, the first trailer remains the most-watched ever (718.6m views in 24 hours, 1B+ in under a week) and tracking models project ~$2.5B worldwide, second only to Avatar: The Way of Water post-COVID. Polymarket gives it ~54.5% to be the year's top domestic film. A five-month post-release window before year-end gives ample runway to clear $1.5B; the principal risk remains reception/word-of-mouth underperforming the hype.
forecasts.base_rate: Recent flagship MCU Spider-Man films (No Way Home ~$1.9B) cleared $1.5B; tentpole superhero sequels with massive pre-release interest usually reach this tier, though not universally.

factors_up.factor: Record-shattering trailer engagement and ~$2.5B tracking signalling enormous demand
Confirmed late-July release leaves ~5 months of box-office runway before year-end

factors_down.factor: Hype does not always convert to gross; weak reviews could cap the run
$1.5B is a high bar only a handful of films reach

key_uncertainties: Critical reception and word of mouth
China and international rollout strength
Competition in the summer/autumn slate

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Holds at 99% (near-certain). Late-May 2026 reporting puts Anthropic at a ~$47B run rate and OpenAI at roughly $25-33B, already summing to ~$72-80B on headline figures before two more quarters of growth. Even under OpenAI's disputed downward recalculation of Anthropic's number (~$8B lower), the combined total needs only modest H2 growth to clear $70B, and the headline reported figures already exceed the bar.
forecasts.base_rate: Once a fast-growing metric has already exceeded a threshold, the probability of the year-end reading also exceeding it is very high absent a collapse.

factors_up.factor: Combined reported run-rate already ~$72-80B at mid-2026, above the $70B bar
Both firms growing rapidly with strong enterprise demand and imminent IPOs

factors_down.factor: Accounting disputes (gross vs net) could lower the credited Anthropic figure
Possible demand or pricing shock in H2 2026

key_uncertainties: Which ARR definition (gross vs net) the resolving source uses
Reliability/timing of Q4 2026 disclosures
Any sharp H2 deceleration
update_triggers: Q4 2026 ARR disclosures from either firm

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Roughly steady at 34%. The OBR's March 2026 outlook still implies trend real GDP growth around 1.5%: productivity is assumed to recover to ~1% in the medium term while labour-supply growth falls to ~0.5% by 2030 on lower migration and ageing, with real GDP per person averaging ~1.1%/yr to 2030. That leaves a full-decade average above 1.5% as roughly a coin-flip tilted slightly below threshold, given the OBR's repeated downgrades and persistent productivity disappointment.
forecasts.base_rate: UK per-person growth has averaged near zero since 2019 and well below the pre-2008 ~2% trend; official long-run projections have repeatedly been revised down.

factors_up.factor: OBR assumes productivity recovers toward ~1%; AI diffusion could add upside late-decade
Population growth adds to headline GDP even where per-person growth is modest

factors_down.factor: Labour-supply growth falling to ~0.5% by 2030 on lower migration and ageing
Track record of persistent productivity underperformance vs forecasts

key_uncertainties: Whether the assumed productivity recovery materialises
Net migration policy and demographic trajectory
Whether AI delivers a measurable late-2030s growth boost
update_triggers: Successive OBR revisions to trend growth
